content:
watchOS 27 is set to launch at the end of this month, and Apple Watch users may notice changes in how some features work. The upcoming software update removes three features that users might find inconvenient after upgrading.

Apple Watch Removes Walkie-Talkie Feature

First up is Walkie-Talkie, Apple's real-time voice communication app that only works between Apple Watches.

For me, Walkie-Talkie was never particularly appealing, especially since a yellow app icon would stay on the watch face permanently once enabled. Users who actually used the feature have already started to miss it, and this month (along with new Apple Watch launches) will see even more people noticing its absence.

I don't think third-party apps can fully replicate Apple's Walkie-Talkie feature on Apple Watch. However, a version that supports both iPhone and Apple Watch would likely be more popular.

Multitasking Shortcut Feature Disappears

Next is the Digital Crown double-click multitasking gesture, which now does the same thing as a single click on the Digital Crown. I mentioned this previously in my watchOS 27 public beta preview and discussed it again yesterday.

I don't know if double-clicking the Digital Crown will become watchOS's multitasking solution in the future. But being able to quickly switch between two apps, or between an app and the watch face, has always been incredibly useful. Hopefully an alternative will return in the future.

As for the double-click button shortcut, I think Apple Watch has limited buttons, and double-click actions should correspond to some function, even if it's not multitasking. I'm now considering these two separately.

Dynamic App List Becomes Default

Finally, let's talk about the change in what shows up when you single-click the Digital Crown.

Since watchOS 1 (then called Watch OS 1), pressing the Digital Crown from either the watch face or within an app would open the full app launcher. The biggest change to this system before now was when Apple removed the design that centered the app list on first press before returning to the watch face.

watchOS 27 changes this to a Dynamic App List: five smart-recommended apps, the Siri app, and an icon for the full app list. You can tap that icon, or scroll up on the Digital Crown to see the full list or app inventory.

I understand the reasoning behind this change. Apps on Apple Watch weren't terribly popular to begin with. The new Dynamic App List offers larger tap targets and reduces the number of icons to browse. It also puts the Siri app in a prominent position, which fits the overall theme of Apple's OS 27 updates.

If I could choose, I would probably turn off the Dynamic App List. It's acceptable as a default, but it feels more cumbersome to operate compared to going straight to the app launcher.

Regardless, any change takes an adjustment period before becoming the new normal. That said, I've been using watchOS 27 since the first day of beta 1 in early June. For me, the loss of Walkie-Talkie isn't that noticeable, the removal of the multitasking shortcut feels temporary, and the Dynamic App List as a default is okay but slightly inconvenient for users who prioritize speed.

Of course, if I could get the Explorer watch face back, I'd accept all of the above changes. Removing features and changing how things work is expected, but removing an Apple Watch face when users can already delete faces themselves is still hard to understand.

Make the most of your Apple products
